entries.content:
Metroids are energy-siphoning predators engineered by the Chozo on the planet SR388. The Thoha tribe of the Chozo, working with Mother Brain, created them to hunt the X Parasite, a shape-stealing organism the Chozo feared would spread beyond SR388. Per the Fusion manual, the word Metroid in the Chozo language translates roughly as "ultimate warrior". The Metroids nearly wiped out the X, then turned feral and became SR388's dominant predator. The Thoha eventually resolved to destroy the planet to be rid of them; Raven Beak of the Mawkin, who coveted Metroids as weapons of galactic conquest, slaughtered the Thoha to stop that plan, sparing only Quiet Robe because only the Thoha could control Metroids.

Essentials (see Metroid biology and weaknesses, Metroid life cycle):
- A larval Metroid is a floating, translucent, jellyfish-like organism with red nuclei and four talon-like claws. It latches onto prey and drains its life energy, leaving a dried husk.
- Metroids shrug off most weapons. The dependable method is to freeze one with the Ice Beam and shatter it with Missiles.
- On SR388 they mature through Alpha, Gamma, Zeta and Omega forms to the egg-laying Queen Metroid. Away from SR388 they ordinarily remain larvae.
- Per the original manual, Metroids multiply when exposed to beta rays for 24 hours.

History in brief. The Galactic Federation collected specimens for research; Space Pirates seized them and bred them on Zebes under Mother Brain, which is what first sent Samus to Zebes. Pirates also carried Metroids to Tallon IV and Aether, where Phazon produced the Tallon, Hunter and Fission strains and, in the Impact Crater, the creature called Metroid Prime (see Metroid variants of the Prime era). After Zebes the Federation ordered the species exterminated at its source, and Samus did so on SR388, destroying every form up to the Queen, but spared a newly hatched larva that imprinted on her (see The baby Metroid). Ridley stole that hatchling from Ceres; it died on Zebes saving Samus from Mother Brain, leaving the species extinct in nature. Federation and Pirate factions alike then tried to recreate Metroids from preserved cells: aboard the Bottle Ship, in the BSL station's Restricted Laboratory, on ZDR under Raven Beak, and in the host-controlling strain Sylux used on Tanamaar and Viewros (see Metroid breeding and cloning programs).

Both the Federation and the Space Pirates prize Metroids as bioweapons; Pirate records on Tallon IV claimed that "a small force of disciplined Metroids could wipe out entire armies". Federation scientists also valued their energy-producing properties, which is why Samus delivered the hatchling to Ceres alive.

Samus has killed more Metroids than anyone and was the Federation's instrument of their extermination, yet she spared the last larva, grieved its death, and owes it her life twice: once in Mother Brain's chamber and once when a vaccine cultured from its cells cured her X infection (Metroid Fusion). Since that vaccine she shares the species' weakness to cold, and after ZDR she carries its energy-draining power (see Samus as the last Metroid).
entries.notes: The 'ultimate warrior' translation is sourced to the Metroid Fusion instruction booklet (p. 40) via Metroid Wiki, not to in-game dialogue. Beta-ray multiplication is from the NES manual and the Zero Mission manual (p. 6).

entries.content:
A Metroid in its common larval form is a floating, jellyfish-like organism: a translucent membrane enclosing red nuclei, with four talon-like claws hanging beneath. The outer claws grip prey; the inner claws draw out its life energy. Samus's Logbook classifies the Metroid as an "energy-based parasitic predator". Space Pirate autopsies on Tallon IV found the internal organs "limited to nucleonic absorption cells and massive energy reservoirs"; the Tallon strain has no discernible sensory organs or circulatory system and feeds through twin mandibles wired by energy conduits to a quadripartite nucleus. Metroids refuse synthetic sustenance and must feed on living prey. Victims are left as desiccated husks, as Samus found strewn through Tourian on Zebes. Feeding makes a Metroid grow, and gorging can kill it. Alone among the strains outside SR388, Metroid Prime and the Ing-possessed Dark Tallon Metroids show a visible eye.

A Metroid attacks by latching onto a target and draining it. Once attached it is nearly impossible to pull off; the proven remedy is a Morph Ball Bomb, which forces it to release.

Weaknesses:
- Cold is the species' mortal weakness. Pirate data records that "temperatures below 10° centigrade will render Metroids docile". A Metroid frozen solid by the Ice Beam shatters under Missiles; a frozen larva of the Zebes stock took five Missiles, a Tallon Metroid only one.
- Ice Missiles, the Dark Beam against Dark Tallon Metroids, and the Nova Beam fired through a Phazon Metroid's core exploit the same vulnerability.
- Omega Metroids are highly resistant to cold; their chest is the vulnerable spot. Alpha, Gamma and Zeta Metroids on SR388 were immune to everything but Missiles.
- Federation genetic manipulation aboard the Bottle Ship produced Metroids said to be unfreezable (see Metroid breeding and cloning programs).

Per the original manual, Metroids in suspended animation reactivate and multiply when exposed to beta rays for 24 hours, which is why the Space Pirates stole the Federation's samples.

Samus has relied on the freeze-and-shatter method since her first Zebes mission. After the Metroid vaccine saved her from the X, the BSL computer warned her, "Like Metroids, you can be frozen by an Ice Beam", and cold-based weapons became a danger to her. In the BSL's Restricted Laboratory the captive Metroids ignored her entirely while swarming the SA-X.
entries.notes: Nucleus count left unstated because sources disagree (three vs four). Omega cold resistance comes from the Metroid Egg stub. Power Bombs are not claimed to kill ordinary larvae since only the Fission Metroid page confirms it.

entries.comment: Metroids: Metroid life cycle (Alpha, Gamma, Zeta, Omega, Queen)
entries.content:
On SR388, and nowhere else naturally, a Metroid passes through a chain of molts that turn a floating larva into a reptilian giant. The manual for Samus's first SR388 mission describes each mutation producing "an even larger and more powerful adversary"; the forms carry Greek-letter names.

- Larva: the jellyfish-like form, hatched from an egg laid and tended by a Queen Metroid. A fully developed larva stops floating and lies motionless for a time before it molts.
- Alpha Metroid: rips its way out of the larval membrane and takes a winged, arthropod-like shape. It flies, attacks by diving and ramming, and falls to a handful of Missiles.
- Gamma Metroid: grows much larger, fires lightning bolts and rams; its head and back are vulnerable to Missiles, and about ten were needed to kill one.
- Zeta Metroid: sheds two legs and becomes an upright, faster, stronger reptilian form that spits energy and rams; only Missiles at the face or back harm it, roughly twenty.
- Omega Metroid: huge, highly resistant to cold, nearly full-grown (see Omega Metroid).
- Queen Metroid: an Omega carrying a specific gene matures into the egg-laying Queen, roughly twice an Omega's size (see Metroid Queen). Because the gene is rare, few Metroids ever reach the end of the cycle; most Samus has met were larvae or adolescents.

The cycle depends on SR388 itself. The hatchling Samus carried away from the planet grew enormous but never molted, because away from SR388 it could not follow the normal growth cycle. When the Galactic Federation wanted Alpha, Gamma, Zeta and Omega Metroids for its secret BSL program, it had to build "a faithful replica of the SR388 ecosystem", and its researchers developed rapid-growth techniques said to raise an Omega from a larva within days. Separately, per the original manual, larvae in suspended animation multiply when exposed to beta rays for 24 hours; that is reproduction, not maturation.

Samus is the only person known to have fought every form. During the extermination of SR388 she destroyed sixteen Gamma, three Zeta and four Omega Metroids on her way down to the Queen (Metroid II). The only grown Metroids she has seen since were the captive Alpha, Gamma and Zeta specimens in the BSL's Restricted Laboratory, the Omega that met her at the BSL docking bay, and the Queen the Federation raised aboard the Bottle Ship.
entries.notes: Counts of Gamma/Zeta/Omega are from the Metroid II pages; Samus Returns may differ (Metroid Wiki trivia says 50 Metroids total vs 39). The 'Beta Metroid' mentioned only on the Metroid Egg stub was omitted as unverified in any game.

entries.comment: Metroids: Metroid variants of the Prime era (Tallon, Hunter, Fission, Phazon Metroids, Hatcher)
entries.content:
Outside SR388 Metroids never follow their natural life cycle, but Space Pirate research and Phazon exposure produced a family of mutant strains that Samus catalogued in her Logbook across the Phazon crisis.

- Tallon Metroid: the strain that developed after the Pirates shipped Metroids from Zebes to the Glacier One laboratories in Phendrana Drifts on Tallon IV. Smaller and weaker than the Zebes stock (a frozen one shatters under a single Missile), it feeds through twin mandibles linked to a quadripartite nucleus. Phazon infusion trials increased mass and aggression and mutated the mandibles, but also caused organ degeneration and deaths. On Aether the Pirates bred Tallon Metroids in artificial cocoons for bio-energy; the Aether-raised ones are red. Pirate Metroid Handling Protocols forbade keeping them as pets after failed domestication killed several handlers, and a Pirate theft report blamed Dark Samus for missing Metroids.
- Infant Tallon Metroid: docile hatchlings the Pirates carried in cocoons as portable "organic batteries"; on contact with Phazon they mature rapidly into full Tallon Metroids.
- Hunter Metroid: a further development seen in the Phazon Mines and Phendrana's Frost Cave. "Quick to anger", it charges prey to ram it and drains energy at range through a long tentacle. Cold still subdues it.
- Fission Metroid: found in the Phazon Core of the Impact Crater, a mutant "capable of splitting in two"; each half becomes invulnerable to all but the beam matching its colour (yellow Power, purple Wave, white Ice, red Plasma), a randomness attributed to Phazon's chaotic mutation. A Power Bomb or the Phazon Beam destroys one instantly.
- Dark Tallon Metroid: Tallon Metroids possessed by Ing darklings on Dark Aether, "powerful soldiers of the Horde" even though Metroids attack Ing on sight. The Light Beam harms them; the Dark Beam freezes them for Missiles.
- Phazon Metroid: the adult form of the tiny, flocking Miniroids, bred by the Pirates and native to Phaaze. It phases through solid matter, discharges Phazon bursts and drains prey; Ice Missiles immobilise it and the Nova Beam through its core kills it in one shot. Samus first met them in tanks in SkyTown on Elysia and later in holding cells with eggs on the Pirate Homeworld.
- Hopping Metroid: a strain that lost flight and runs on legs edged with Phazite, able to enter Hypermode; seen at Norion's Cargo Dock B and on Phaaze.
- Metroid Hatcher: a floating head with four energy-leeching tentacles and a Phazite-hard shell protecting its heart. Unable to phase, it spawns Phazon Metroids from its mouth and dies once every tentacle is torn off. Samus fought Hatchers at Norion's Generator B, in the Metroid Creche of the Pirate Homeworld and aboard the GFS Valhalla.

The most extreme Phazon mutation, the guardian creature in Tallon IV's Impact Crater, is covered under Metroid Prime (the creature); its remnant became Dark Samus.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki's Hunter Metroid page lists no Prime 3 appearance, so none is claimed. Phazon Metroid egg-laying without a Queen is reported as 'reportedly' on the wiki and was left out.

entries.content:
The baby Metroid, also called the hatchling or simply "the baby" (Samus's own word for it), was the last Metroid born on SR388. Its egg hatched in front of Samus moments after she destroyed the Queen Metroid at the bottom of the planet. Per the Other M manual, "As I was the first thing the baby saw, it took me to be its mother." Ordered to exterminate every Metroid, Samus could not bring herself to kill it; it followed her toward the surface and cleared obstacles from her path (Metroid II). When Proteus Ridley ambushed her at the landing site to seize it, the hatchling drained Ridley's energy and poured it into Samus, letting her beat him off.

Samus delivered it to the Galactic Research Station at Ceres, where scientists determined that its energy-producing qualities could benefit civilization. For a brief moment, in the words of the record of those days, "The last Metroid is in captivity. The galaxy is at peace." Shortly after Samus left, the scientists were slaughtered and Ridley carried the hatchling off to the rebuilt Space Pirate base on Zebes.

On Zebes, after killing Ridley in Norfair, Samus found the hatchling's container broken in two. In Tourian, among the husks of drained creatures, she met a Metroid far larger than any larva she had seen: the baby, which had kept growing without molting because it was away from SR388. It drained her almost to death before recognising her, then fled. In Mother Brain's chamber, as Mother Brain's Hyper Beam was killing Samus, the hatchling returned, latched onto Mother Brain and drained her, then transferred the stolen energy into Samus, healing her. Mother Brain recovered and shot the baby to pieces; its remains fell onto Samus and gave her the Hyper Beam, with which she destroyed Mother Brain. Its death left the species extinct in nature. It never grew past the larval form, so its sex is unknown.

Its cells outlived it. A culture the Galactic Federation preserved became the vaccine that saved Samus from the X; cells salvaged from her Power Suit seeded the Bottle Ship's cloned Metroids; and the "Baby's Cry" distress signal that drew her to the Bottle Ship was named for it (see Metroid breeding and cloning programs). During the BSL incident Samus stated, "I owe the Metroid hatchling my life twice over", and aboard the Bottle Ship she was reminded of it constantly; she still longs for it.
entries.notes: Selective entry: bare 'hatchling'/'the baby' require a disambiguating secondary key. 'The last Metroid is in captivity. The galaxy is at peace.' is the Super Metroid opening narration, verified via web search.

entries.content:
The Queen Metroid is the final form of the Metroid life cycle and the only Metroid that lays eggs; a Queen propagates the entire species. Only an Omega Metroid carrying a specific gene can mature into one, which makes Queens rare, as Samus noted aboard the Bottle Ship. A Queen is roughly twice the size of an Omega: a vast armoured bulk with three-clawed paws and a long neck she extends to bite or ram. She spits bursts of energy, and her face, neck and the inside of her stomach are her vulnerable points; Missiles, Morph Ball Bombs and Power Bombs can hurt her. She lays her eggs in a nest and tends them; a fully developed larva hatches from the egg and, on SR388, goes on to become an Alpha Metroid.

The SR388 Queen. During her extermination mission Samus found the Queen at the deepest point of the planet's caverns, past the Omega Metroids guarding the approach. She pounded the Queen's face with Missiles, stunned her with a Missile fired into her open mouth, then rolled into the Queen's gullet in Morph Ball and detonated Bombs inside her. The Queen's death should have ended the species; instead one last egg hatched in front of Samus and the hatchling imprinted on her (see The baby Metroid).

The Bottle Ship Queen (Metroid: Other M). Galactic Federation researchers, cloning Metroids from cells the Federation had salvaged, genetically manipulated hatchling clones so that at least one could grow into a Queen, and used her as a control specimen for their cold-resistant Metroids. This Queen killed the Bottle Ship's Ridley clone. In the Bioweapon Research Center, as the ship bore down on Federation-controlled orbit, a scientist opened the hatch onto the Queen's chamber; Samus fought her, used the Grapple Beam to pull herself into the Queen's mouth and set off a Power Bomb in her stomach.

Samus is the only known person to have killed a Queen Metroid, and she has done it twice. Metroid eggs have otherwise been seen in the Space Pirates' Phazon Metroid holding cells on the Pirate Homeworld and in Galactic Federation storage, where Sylux hacked open a stasis tube to hatch one (see Metroid breeding and cloning programs).
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki's Queen page gives no Samus Returns-specific encounter details, so the SR388 account follows the Metroid II description.

entries.content:
The Omega Metroid is the largest growth form of the Metroid life cycle, the molt that follows the Zeta and precedes the Queen. Omegas are nearly full-grown Metroids; those carrying a specific gene mature into Queens. The manual for Samus's first SR388 mission describes the Omega as "absolutely huge; its power, incredible!" It is a towering bipedal reptilian with massive claws, highly resistant to cold, and it attacks with energy bursts, by ramming and by slashing. Its chest is the vulnerable point; the Omegas of SR388 were immune to everything but Missiles, and Samus needed some thirty Missiles to the chest or back to bring one down.

On SR388 four Omega Metroids held the deepest caverns just above the Queen's nest, and Samus destroyed all four during the extermination mission (Metroid II). Within the Galactic Federation's secret program aboard the BSL research station, the station computer boasted that its replica of SR388's ecosystem was "ideal for raising Alpha, Gamma, Zeta, and even Omega Metroids" and that rapid-growth techniques could take a larva to Omega within days.

The BSL Omega. At the end of the BSL incident Samus reached the docking bay to find her gunship gone and an Omega Metroid in its place. At that moment it was invulnerable to every weapon she carried, and it clawed her down to the edge of death. An SA-X attacked and wounded it, only to be killed by the Omega; Samus absorbed the SA-X's Core-X, recovered the Ice Beam and destroyed the Omega with it, the cold the species fears being its undoing (Metroid Fusion). The full account belongs under Omega Metroid of the BSL.

No Omega Metroid existed on ZDR; the Metroid power that awoke in Samus there was her own (see Samus as the last Metroid). Samus knows the Omega as the last barrier before a Queen and as the only Metroid that has ever stood over her with her weapons useless.
entries.notes: Verified: Metroid Wiki's Omega Metroid page and the Dread page record no Omega Metroid in Dread. Bipedal/clawed description is drawn from the page's artwork and the Fusion encounter; the page itself has no prose description.

entries.comment: Metroids: Metroid breeding and cloning programs
entries.content:
Every power that has handled Metroids has tried to breed them, and every program has ended in Samus's hands.

Space Pirates. The original Pirate plan on Zebes was to multiply the Galactic Federation's stolen specimens by beta-ray exposure (per the original manual) and use them as biological weapons; Samus destroyed the Metroids of Tourian. The Pirates' first attempt at Metroid clones, the Mochtroids of Maridia, could drain energy but could not latch onto prey, and their fragile bodies died easily (per the manual of the Zebes mission). On Tallon IV and Aether the Pirates ran Phazon infusion trials, bred Tallon Metroids in cocoons for bio-energy and wrote Metroid Handling Protocols after domestication killed handlers; on the Pirate Homeworld they kept Phazon Metroids and their eggs in a Metroid Creche (see Metroid variants of the Prime era).

The Bottle Ship. The Federation reproduced Metroids "from a piece of cell structure salvaged by the Federation", material taken from Samus's Power Suit after the baby's death on Zebes. They were kept in Sector Zero, a unit absent from the ship's map data. Genetic manipulation reportedly overcame "the Metroid's mortal weakness, the vulnerability to cold", making the adults unfreezable, though infants had not yet grown into that immunity. Because the first hatchling had to recognise its mother, the Federation built MB, an android carrying Mother Brain's thought patterns, to control the Metroids; the colony also produced a Queen Metroid. Adam Malkovich detached and detonated Sector Zero, dying with the Metroids and ending the program.

The BSL station. The station computer told Samus, "the Federation has been secretly working on a Metroid breeding program. For peaceful application only, of course." In the Restricted Laboratory, within a replica of SR388's ecosystem, researchers raised larvae and Alpha, Gamma and Zeta Metroids and developed rapid-growth techniques. An SA-X broke in; the captive Metroids ignored Samus and swarmed the X mimic, the laboratory was jettisoned and exploded, and only Samus's account of it survives.

ZDR. Raven Beak had meant to bring Metroids to ZDR; after Samus exterminated them he reprogrammed the E.M.M.I. units to harvest her Metroid DNA, intending to clone an army of the most powerful Metroid from her. He died with his planet.

Sylux. Sylux had earlier hacked open a stasis tube holding a Metroid egg in a Federation research station. Per Nintendo's official account, "Metroid eggs secretly stored in a certain research center of the Galactic Federation were forcibly hatched" by Sylux, who exploited the imprinting instinct of newborn Metroids, gave them "a new ability - to merge with and control other organisms", and controlled officer-class Space Pirates through them. These host-fusing Metroids struck the Federation facility on Tanamaar, fused with the Pirate Aberax, and were carried with everything else to Viewros (Metroid Prime 4: Beyond).

Samus has destroyed, or watched the destruction of, every one of these programs she has found. The Federation's secrecy at the BSL drove her to defy its orders outright (see Samus's defiance of the Federation at the BSL).
entries.notes: Sylux quotes are from a Nintendo Today app entry as quoted by Nintendo World Report. The link between the Federation Force egg and the Prime 4 Metroids is the wiki's/author's inference, so the entry states both facts without asserting they are the same egg. Nintendo Life calls Sylux's creatures Mochtroids; Metroid Wiki calls them modified Metroids; the entry uses the official 'merge with and control' wording.

entries.comment: Metroids: Samus as the last Metroid
entries.content:
"The last Metroid is in captivity. The galaxy is at peace." Those words marked the delivery of the SR388 hatchling to Ceres; when Mother Brain killed it on Zebes, the Metroid species was extinct in the wild. Every Metroid since has been grown from preserved cells, and every such colony has been destroyed. What remains of the species lives in Samus Aran.

The vaccine. When an X Parasite infected Samus on SR388, the Galactic Federation "had managed to preserve a cell culture from the last infant Metroid" and injected her with a serum made from it. The Metroid cells overran and destroyed the X, transformed her Power Suit by giving it Metroid properties, and left her able to absorb free X and vulnerable to cold like any Metroid (see Fusion Suit; Samus Aran – Metroid DNA, Chozo DNA and what she has become). Per the Fusion manual, "As the inheritor of the Metroids' powers, Samus becomes the only being capable of opposing the X parasite horde"; by the Chozo meaning of the name, she became the last "ultimate warrior". In the BSL's Restricted Laboratory, captive Metroids ignored her and attacked the SA-X instead. She has said she owes the hatchling her life twice over.

ZDR. Raven Beak lured Samus to ZDR to extract her Metroid DNA and clone an army from it, and his reprogrammed E.M.M.I. hunted her for that DNA. As the X were loosed from Elun, the Metroid DNA within her began to awaken: she manifested an energy-sapping power, used it to consume the last E.M.M.I., and was slowly turning into a Metroid. Raven Beak revealed he had spared her so that this power would mature before he cloned her at full strength. On Itorash, near death, her Metroid nature fully awoke; her suit took on a Metroid-like form (see Metroid Suit), she drained Raven Beak and the energy of Itorash itself, sending the ship crashing into ZDR, and destroyed the X that had seized Raven Beak's body. At her gunship, Adam warned her that touching the controls would drain the ship. An X mimicking Quiet Robe bowed to her and let itself be absorbed, stabilising her Metroid DNA so that she could fly (Metroid Dread).

Status. SR388 and the BSL were destroyed together, the Bottle Ship's colony died with Sector Zero, and ZDR exploded behind her; Sylux's host-fusing Metroids on Viewros date, per developer statements, to the years before the BSL incident. Samus's transformation was halted but not undone: she carries human, Chozo and Metroid heritage, cold remains her weakness, and no other Metroid is known to survive. Raven Beak saw in her the most powerful Metroid that could exist; how she herself regards that is covered under Samus Aran – Metroid DNA, Chozo DNA and what she has become.
entries.notes: Dread final-battle dialogue could not be verified verbatim from any reachable source, so Raven Beak's words are paraphrased. 'Slowly becoming a Metroid' follows Wikipedia's wording. The Prime 4 chronological placement (between Super Metroid and Fusion) is from Nintendo World Report's paraphrase of a Famitsu developer interview.

result.research_notes: Could not verify: (1) verbatim Raven Beak/Adam dialogue from Dread's ending (Metroid Wiki's Dread, Raven Beak, Quiet Robe pages and Wikipedia/Inverse give only paraphrase; Looper fetch returned an index page; Itorash page 404). (2) Metroid Wiki's Metroid (species) page has no Dread or Prime 4 sections; Dread/Prime 4 Metroid facts come from Wikipedia, the Metroid Wiki Dread/Raven Beak/Quiet Robe/Sylux pages and the Nintendo Today text quoted by Nintendo World Report. (3) Samus Returns Metroid counts: Metroid Wiki trivia says 50 appear vs 39 in Metroid II; stage counts in the life-cycle entry are Metroid II figures. (4) 'Ultimate warrior' is from the Fusion manual p. 40 (and Metroid Wiki's framing that Samus is 'the last ultimate warrior' is editorial); no in-game line confirmed. (5) Omega Metroid cold resistance and 'Beta Metroid' come only from the Metroid Egg stub; Beta omitted. (6) The claim that Sector Zero was a 'replica of Tourian' and that '33 Metroids survived' in Fusion appeared only in the first summary of the species page and were not corroborated, so both were omitted. (7) Conflict: Nintendo Life calls Sylux's Prime 4 creatures Mochtroids, Metroid Wiki calls them a new modified Metroid strain, Nintendo Today describes forcibly hatched Federation-stored eggs given a merge-and-control ability; the entries follow the official Nintendo Today wording. (8) The link between the Federation Force post-credits egg and Prime 4's Metroids is inference by Metroid Wiki/NWR, stated as two separate facts. Pages that 404'd on Metroid Wiki: Larva_Metroid, Metroid_(larva), Metroid_vaccine (lowercase; Metroid_Vaccine worked), Metroid_Creche, Itorash. Wikitroid not attempted.
